title: Throughput Safeguard & Scaling Heuristic Engine
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a robust autoscaling policy engine component that translates observed workload signals into safe, throughput-guaranteed scaling actions for Dedicated capacity. This work focuses on: target metric definitions (throughput target, p95 latency, queue depth, GPU utilization), the set of scaling algorithms to support (threshold, PID controller, rate-limited proportional, and a predictive model prototype), and explicit safety limits (min/max replicas, surge windows, cooldowns, step caps, budget-aware fallback). The goal is an engine that can declaratively express intent (e.g., "maintain 10K reqs/min with p95 < 120ms") and compile that into deterministic actions with observable safety guarantees. This ticket covers the policy DSL surface, the decision-cycle semantics, conflict-resolution rules when multiple policies apply, and a staged rollout plan with simulation and canary metrics. Excludes long-term ML model training pipeline (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL supports expressing target throughputs, latency SLOs, and cost-prioritized preferences
Engine exposes at least three algorithms (threshold, PID, predictive-prototype) selectable per policy
Safety limits enforced: configurable min/max nodes, surge cap, cooldown window, and per-policy emergency disable
Simulation harness demonstrates stable convergence on synthetic workloads (3 patterns: steady increase, diurnal burst, sudden spike) with no violation of min-node constraints
Runtime exposes decision trace events for every scaling action (inputs, selected algorithm, proposed delta, safety clamp, final action) to Console for debugging
End-to-end canary rollout (10% traffic, 24h) shows no customer-visible error-rate increase and meets throughput target for 90% of windows
implementation_notes: Design component: 'intent-translator' converts policy DSL to a prioritized decision graph
Decision cadence: default 15s evaluation window with configurable aggregation (p95/mean/q95 over 1m/5m)
Algorithms: implement baseline threshold and PID in runtime; integrate predictive prototype behind a feature flag
Safety: implement a two-layer guard - (1) per-policy clamps, (2) fleet-wide surge governor with token bucket allowance
Persistence: policy definitions stored in Console DB; engine reads with versioned snapshots to allow rollbacks
Observability: add decision-trace events, synthetic workload simulation dashboard, and a regression test that runs after infra changes
